resources.string: Workspace, paths, backends, approvals and network

What the agent in this chat can read and write right now, who runs its commands, when it asks you, and which networks it can reach. This page only describes the current state; each tool call is checked when it runs.
File tools and built-in commands both use it as their root. Switch it in the workspace bar above.
Files deleted by file tools go to the recycle bin, with version history
No recycle bin or version history. Use Git to review changes
Included in local and WebDAV backups
Termux can open it directly (after termux-setup-storage)
Deleted when &brand; is uninstalled or its data is cleared
The same path means different things to different runners: / is the workspace for file tools, the device root for commands and Termux, and the remote root over SSH.
File tools and sandboxed scripts: the workspace root
Built-in commands: the same workspace, also their working directory
Your skills folder. Every change asks for approval; commands use $NEXARA_SKILLS
No external folders mounted. Add one under External folders on the Files page
Only file tools and sandboxed scripts can open it; commands cannot see it
Files that commands delete or overwrite skip the recycle bin. Turn on and manage Termux and SSH in tool settings.
Run as &brand; in the workspace and can also read and write &brand;\'s own data
Isolated process; reaches the workspace only through file approvals
Runs in the Termux home folder and cannot see this workspace; exchange files through a mount or shared storage
Runs in the Termux home folder; this workspace is in shared storage, so Termux can open it
Connects only to hosts saved in settings; the remote account decides what it can touch
System shell only; no built-in Python on this device
JavaScript only; no built-in Python on this device
In every mode, SSH host changes, skills folder changes, permanent deletes and new scheduled tasks ask each time.
Tools run directly; only the exceptions below ask you
Reads run directly; writes, deletes, commands, scripts, external writes and MCP tools ask you
